questions.q: What does Anthropic's own documentation say about Claude and images?
options: Claude can both understand and generate images
Claude is an image understanding model only — it cannot generate, produce, edit, or create images
Claude can generate images but not read them
Claude has no image capability of any kind
questions.explain: Anthropic documents Claude as image understanding only; image generation is a separate capability Claude does not have.

questions.q: Which OpenAI image model variant is tuned for precise, iterative editing rather than fast one-shot generation?
options: Flare
DALL-E 3
Sunburst
Realtime-2
questions.explain: GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst is tuned for editing precision; Flare is tuned for fast, high-quality everyday generation.

questions.q: What is Google's current native image-generation capability inside Gemini called?
options: Imagen 4 (standalone endpoint)
Nano Banana / Nano Banana Pro
Gemini Realtime
DALL-E for Gemini
questions.explain: Nano Banana and Nano Banana Pro are Gemini's native image-generation capability; the older standalone Imagen generation endpoints have been wound down.

questions.q: What makes xAI's Aurora engine (behind Grok Imagine) notable among image-generation approaches?
options: It is autoregressive — predicting the image piece by piece — rather than diffusion-based
It only produces black-and-white images
It requires no prompt at all
It can only run on xAI's own hardware
questions.explain: Most image models (GPT Image 2.5, Nano Banana) are diffusion-based; Aurora instead predicts the image piece by piece, an autoregressive approach closer in spirit to next-token text prediction.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say vision and image generation 'don't imply each other'?
options: Because they are actually the exact same capability under a different name
Because only Google offers either capability
Because a provider offering one capability may not offer the other — Claude reads images but does not generate them
Because generation always requires vision to work first
questions.explain: Claude is the clearest example: strong image understanding, zero image-generation capability. A capable vision model is not automatically a capable image generator, or vice versa.
